name: Chinese · Phrases · Feelings, thanks and apologies
source: Phrases: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org) sentences written by native speakers, each linked in its src; lines marked generated were written for Lianki and checked for natural use

entries.note: Thanking a group: after a speech, a party or help from colleagues.
The standard reply to thanks; friends often say 没事 instead.
Reply to thanks or an apology among friends; also 'I'm fine'.
Stronger than 谢谢, for a real favour.
After asking a favour, before it's done; common in messages.
Often used to politely decline an offer.

entries.back: Please don't go to any trouble.
entries.note: Declining an offer of help, food or a lift.
Modest reply to a compliment, instead of 'thank you'.
Arriving late to a meeting, class or dinner.
For small inconveniences: bumping someone, making them wait.
A sincere apology after an argument, to a partner or friend.

entries.reading: nǐ bié shēng wǒ de qì a
entries.back: Please don't be mad at me.
entries.note: Pleading, softened by 啊; to a friend or partner.

entries.term: 给你添麻烦了，真的非常抱歉。
entries.reading: gěi nǐ tiān máfan le，zhēn de fēicháng bàoqiàn
entries.back: Sorry for all the trouble I've caused you.
entries.note: A serious apology, e.g. to a host, colleague or client.

entries.reading: méi guānxi，bié fàng zài xīn shàng
entries.back: It's fine, don't worry about it.
entries.note: Accepting an apology and telling them to let it go.
After someone trips, looks upset or goes quiet.
Reassuring a worried friend.
New job, wedding, baby, passed exam.
Reacting to good news.
Plain, heartfelt joy.
To a friend who's grinning or humming.
About a kind gesture, gift or story.
Literally 'tired to death'; flopping down after a long day.
Venting about someone or something that infuriated you.
About noise, a person or a hassle.
Snapping at someone who keeps bothering you; blunt.
Before an exam, interview or performance.
When someone startles you, or after a near miss.
Friendly envy at someone's trip, job or luck; not bitter.
Missing out on something, or someone else's bad luck.

entries.back: I really can't take it anymore.
entries.note: At the end of your patience with a person or situation.
Disbelief at what someone just said or did.
